articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot gets social-engineered into handing over Obama and Space Force Instagram accounts to Iranian hackers. When your AI is dumber than a Telegram script kiddie, maybe it's time to reconsider automation.

articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually uploads AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets to public GitHub repo because apparently cybersecurity agencies don't practice what they preach. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a zero-day exploit.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification schemes are creating a privacy nightmare for everyone while lawmakers pretend they're protecting kids. Spoiler alert: surveillance capitalism doesn't suddenly become wholesome when you slap a 'for the children' label on it.

articles.title: Global Stock Exchange Hit by Monthslong Email Campaign
articles.summary: Police using license plate readers for school residency checks and noise complaints because nothing says 'protect and serve' like turning every traffic camera into a panopticon. Mission creep is the feature, not the bug.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philly cops admit they're tracking social media posts critical of AI data centers as 'First Amendment activity.' When your constitutional rights become police surveillance categories, democracy has left the building.

articles.title: Claude celebrates Anthropic's stock market float with blockbuster ... outage
articles.summary: Microsoft walks back threats against 0-day researchers after security community collectively tells them to touch grass. Nothing like public humiliation to remind corporations that shooting the messenger is bad PR.

articles.title: New HTTP/2 Bomb Vulnerability Allows Remote DoS on NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy & Cloudflare
articles.summary: Unpatched Windows Search URI vulnerability lets attackers steal NTLMv2 hashes because Microsoft's commitment to security is like their commitment to user privacy: purely theoretical.

articles.title: Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users, CountLoader Hits 86K, Miners Spread via Pirated Content
articles.summary: New HTTP/2 Bomb vulnerability can remotely DoS NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, and Cloudflare. When one exploit can take down the entire web server ecosystem, you know we've achieved true digital fragility.

articles.title: Anthropic is finally giving the EU access to Mythos, ending weeks of standoff over the world’s most powerful cybersecurity AI
articles.summary: 9.8-rated Windows Server vulnerability grants system privileges with a single malformed packet and domain controllers are getting pwned in the wild. Microsoft's security model: why make it hard when you can make it impossible?

articles.title: (2026.06.02) (various)
articles.summary: Anthropic finally gives EU access to Mythos AI after weeks of standoff over the model that found 10,000+ zero-days across major operating systems. When your bug-hunting AI is more effective than entire security teams, maybe humans should take notes.
